thread.title: Just How Much Money Could Apple Make by Switching to Its Own Mac Chips?

author: thestreet.com
title: Just How Much Money Could Apple Make by Switching to Its Own Mac Chips?
text:
Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) is well-known for its enormous cash pile and strong earnings but just how much could it benefit from manufacturing its own computer chips?
Reports surfaced Monday, April 2, that Apple was considering creating its own chips for its Mac computers starting in 2020 . The news sent shares of current Apple processor supplier Intel Corp. ( INTC ) plummeting 6% on Monday, while Apple fell 0.7% on a day that saw a route of tech shares.
According to analysts at RBC Capital Markets, Apple could see earnings benefit in the range of 20 cents to 25 cents a share from moving processors in house. That would be about a 2% increase over what FactSet analysts forecast Apple will earn in 2020, when the tech giant would begin making its own chips.
RBC noted that analysts think Apple making its own chips is a "low probability event," but the potential of such a move alone is enough to provide Apple with gross margin tailwinds through either more advantageous negotiations with Intel or through cheaper costs should Apple actually follow through on these reported plans.
"Even though the incremental EPS impact isn't significant, the potential move could enable AAPL to better differentiate its Mac line up vs. PCs," RBC wrote. "Designing its own chips enable AAPL to determine a technological roadmap for Macs that is interdependent of INTC."
The capacity to design its own chips could mean Apple pivots to focus more on augmented and virtual reality technology in its Macs, increased artificial intelligence workloads and a more seamless relationship among all Apple products from Mac to iPhone to iPad, RBC noted.
Analysts added, though, that an Apple-designed, Apple-produced Mac processor would be "technically complex and likely not be immediate." Apple produces about 19 million Mac units, and the mix of Intel i7 and i5 processors is about 35% and 65%, respectively. Apple buys those chips at about a 15% to 20% discount from Intel's chip retail price of between $200 and $300.
All in all, RBC analysts said Apple could benefit from a number of tailwinds including gross margin upsides from lower costs and yield efficiencies, services growth that could contribute to sales and increase gross margins between 50 and 60 basis points, and capital allocation that could stoke between 500 and 600 basis points of share reduction annually through the next five years or more.
Shares of Action Alerts PLUS holding Apple gained 0.55% to $167.60 in premarket trading on Tuesday, April 3.
